chapter_theme: The path of the good son (சற்புத்திர மார்க்கம்), traditionally kiriyai: worship, recitation, praise, chanting, truthfulness and purity offered to the Lord as a son serves a father. Bowing at Hara's feet is the fruit of birth, his feet are the shore for all souls, and he comes forth each time he is worshipped.
structure_note: 1495 places the path among the others (the saha path and sanmarga); 1496 lists its acts; 1497 rebukes those who will not take even a small step; 1498 to 1500 give the reward and the manner of worship; 1501 calls the world to hear it.

1495.reading: The true work of the good son's path is one thing, the saha path's is another; passing beyond both, to become one with the Goddess of the saha path is the clarity of sanmarga.
1495.nuance: சகமார்க்கம் (the companion's path) is traditionally yoga, and சன்மார்க்கம் (the true path) is jnana, so the verse ranks kiriyai, yoga and jnana. தாவிப்பதாம் and சகத்தொழில் are obscure: 'what leaps' or 'what raises', and 'the companion's work' or 'worldly work'. The union with the Goddess (தேவியோடு ஒன்றல்) as the mark of jnana is unusual and may be read of Shakti as grace.

1496.reading: Worshipping, reciting, praising, chanting, faultless good austerity, truthfulness, freedom from impurity, offering food with love and performing the purifications: this is the faultless path of the good son.
1496.nuance: The list mixes ritual acts (pūjā, recitation, japa, food offering, purification) with moral ones (truthfulness, purity), so kiriyai here is not ritual alone. நீசுத்தி is read as the purifications done before worship; the line is compressed.

1497.reading: Even seeing the six-legged bee roam choosing blossoms and the grey swan gather fragrant lotus and blue lily, people do not join even a small path of virtue.
1497.nuance: The plain sense contrasts creatures that gather flowers with people who will not gather them for worship. மறுகா (unwavering) and குறுகா (not shrinking, unfading) are uncertain in what they qualify, and சிறுகால் may mean 'a small path' or 'even for a little while'.

1498.reading: The rare shore is the shade of his feet, the great shore is Pinakan's command, and for all souls who come toward the shore he became the one shore, equal to the seven worlds.
1498.nuance: கரை (shore) is said four times; the sea it implies is birth, which the verse doesn't name. பிஞ்ஞகன் is a name of Siva. Making his ஆணை (command, rule) a shore puts obedience beside refuge.

1499.reading: Rising, bowing, taking up, embracing and marvelling, do service in due order to Hara's feet; done in awe, that is the fruit of birth, and if you part from it in fear, that nature is yours.
1499.nuance: The first line is a string of bodily acts of devotion; முகந்து may be 'taking up' (flowers or water) or 'facing'. The last line, பயந்து பிரிக்கில் அப்பான்மை உனாமே, is obscure: perhaps a warning that whoever separates himself out of fear keeps his bound nature.

1500.reading: Standing I worship, lying down I worship our Lord, always I worship the beautiful supreme light; worship him strewing flowers thick, and each time you worship the Lord of the gods comes forth and appears.
1500.nuance: நின்று, கிடந்து (standing, lying) cover every posture of the day, so worship is unbroken. The promise is plain: he appears (வெளிப்படும்) at each act of worship, not only at its end.

1501.reading: You who live in the world in bodies, hear the sariyai of the good son's path where fortune abides: worship so that the bond that fixes you in the womb shrinks, and stay in joy every day.
1501.nuance: சற்புத்திர மார்க்கச் சரியை reflects the tradition that each path has four grades (the sariyai within kiriyai and so on). கைகூம்ப may mean the bond 'folds' or shrinks, or that one worships with hands folded. கருமன்னு பாசம் is read as the bond that keeps one returning to the womb.

links.note: Both make reaching the Lord's feet the crossing of a sea. The Kural names the great sea of births; Tirumular names only the shore, four times over, and makes it both the shade of the feet and the Lord's command.

The Kural calls a head that does not bow to the Lord's feet as useless as a sense that cannot sense; Tirumular says bowing and serving at Hara's feet is the very fruit of birth. One states the loss, the other the gain.
Both make the Lord answer worship itself: 1500 says he comes forth each time one worships, 1505 that he stands held by the great love of those who make him their eye.
